newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea confident EU to drop anti-dumping measures.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea confident EU to drop anti-dumping measures.

text.p: The Korea Semiconductor Industry Association (KSIA) said on Saturday it was confident the European Union Commission would scrap anti-dumping regulations against South Korean DRAMs for less stringent measures.

Currently South Korean DRAM (dynamic random access memory) makers are forbidden from selling DRAMs in Europe for less than the reference price. The measure was forced in 1993, resulting from a dumping suit filed by the European Electronic Component Manufacturers Association (EECA) in 1990.
But KSIA said the EECA had agreed in principle to accept South Korea's proposal to drop the regulation and introduce measures that would prevent anti-dumping suits from dragging on.
It also said the EU Commission had told KSIA it had decided to terminate the 1990 anti-dumping suit.
KSIA's proposal stipulates that the Korean companies sued for dumping would submit cost and sales data within two weeks to the EU Commission for a speedy decision.
"The new proposal will help boost South Korean DRAM sales in Europe, and hopefully will set a trend for an atmosphere of free trade of semiconductors," said Choi Hye-bum, director at KSIA.
He added that South Korean DRAM manufacturers hoped a similar agreement could be made with the United States.
"We are waiting for the results of an anti-dumping suit under review by the U.S. Department of Commerce on July 16 and are waiting for good news," said Choi.
The EECA and the KSIA are scheduled to meet in Brussels for a two-day meeting starting July 23 to hammer out details for a new agreement on DRAM anti-dumping.
Semiconductor exports to Europe make up almost 20 percent, or $2.1 billion, of total exports by South Korea's five largest chip makers, Choi said.
